intervention: Double training sampling weight for lifted, held target away from bin, using only original demonstrations
controls: Same initialization, 40 epochs, seed42, lr3e-5, frozen normalization/validation, replacement sampler and total draw count; 0% recovery data
selection: Best original fixed validation MSE; no checkpoint epoch selected by rollout
decision: Keep incumbent ex3.pt and its official result unchanged. Preserve both new 99/100 candidates separately. Weighted transport training did not beat its matched unweighted control (489 vs 490 out of 500); improvements over the initial candidate are small.
findings: Six of nine inspected development transport failures ended farther from the bin while the cube remained near the hand, with substantial mocap/hand lag.
Transport-stage oversampling from 22.5% to 36.7% did not reduce transport failures on the fresh paired set: initial7/control7/focus8.
Most observed improvement over the initial candidate is fewer no-lift failures (6 to 2), rather than better transport.
next_experiment: Expand ordinary successful demonstrations across new initial layouts, retaining consistent expert behavior; old recovery data and mere stage reweighting have not shown benefits.
limits: One training seed, 500 paired new scenes; no causal claim about control lag. Confirmation2000 scenes were not used for this training/diagnosis.
